audit.recode_to: Merge with uzbe1247 'Uzbek' (Glottolog 5.1 lists uzbe1247 as a FAMILY-level node; the language-level code for standard/literary Uzbek is nort2690 [uzn]) into ONE record keyed nort2690, then code it consistently with the sister Turkic rows: fixed final primary (01 001 0001...), strict=False, exceptions=listed-set (unstressed/pre-stressing affixes and enclitics, imperatives/optatives, numerals, interrogatives/adverbs, unassimilated loans, names), citing Kononov 1960:52 §51 + 54-55 §53 (held, open), Sjoberg 1963:24 §2.4121 (held photos), Ido 2025:162-163, Athanasopoulou et al. 2020:2,12; no secondary-stress grid on the rule (Kononov §51's rhythmic secondaries and Raun's hedged s1 secondary go to a caution flag). If instead the catalog's rule is that Sjoberg's 'phonemic' verdict (1963:23) forces exclusion as 'lexical', then uzbe1247's fixed-strict row — whose own domain quote is that very sentence — must be excluded too; the two records cannot both stand.

The Sjoberg 1963 statements that the owner note used to keep the row out (p.23 'Stress is phonemic both on the word level...', p.24 'Generally this falls on the final syllable...', p.29 'may be found on any syllable of the derived stem') are all confirmed verbatim on the held page photos. sources.citation: Athanasopoulou, Angeliki, Irene Vogel & Hossep Dolatian. 2020. Acoustic properties of word and phrasal prominence in Uzbek. Proceedings of the Workshop on Turkic and Languages in Contact with Turkic 5: 1-15. doi:10.3765/ptu.v5i1.4796 (CC BY 4.0; LSA host unreachable from our machine, fetched sources via Wayback snapshot 20240501131557)
sources.quote: p.2: 'Like Turkish, Uzbek is reported to have final lexical stress ... Also like Turkish, Uzbek is reported to have, in addition to its canonical final stress, cases in which stress appears in other positions within a word. Specifically, we find a number of lexical exceptions, including loanwords, function words, and proper names ... In addition, there are certain affixes that may require stress to be placed prior to the final syllable' (pre-stressing -ma NEG, equatives, copular person particles; fn.2: 'there are some reports of secondary stress (Sjoberg 1963:31, Bodrogligeti 2003:37)'). p.12
sources.locator: p.2 §2 (descriptive summary, exx. from Sjoberg 1963:24-5); pp.11-12 §5.3 and §6 Conclusions
sources.note: First systematic acoustic study (8 Tashkent speakers, 3 focus conditions): final syllable longer with a falling contour in all conditions, read by the authors as supporting canonical final lexical stress; directly answers the 'Branch C phrasal-only' worry banked in the owner note and contradicts keeping standard Uzbek out while every sister Turkic row is coded final.
